title: Grateful Dead Live at Red Rocks Ampitheatre on 1982-07-29
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1/Dolby B) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/96k) -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.22 -> FLAC/16
source: (FOB) Sennheiser 421 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-C90/Dolby B)

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1982 show with a rare Crazy Fingers jam and excellent in‑your‑face sound quality, though the pacing feels oddly uneven.
ai_review.review: Reviewers praise the recording’s crystal‑clear, “in‑your‑face” sound that ranks among the best of the 1982 era, making the wild atmosphere of the three‑day Rocks run come through vividly. Musically the concert is noted for a rare return to Crazy Fingers and generally strong playing, but one fan points out an unusual pacing with unexpected song pairings that give the set a slightly disjointed feel.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong recording quality boosts the rating, while the show is good but hampered by odd pacing; limited review count lowers confidence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers describe the sound as “up there with many other great sound ’82 shows” and “in‑your‑face,” indicating a very clear, well‑balanced capture.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Unusual song transitions (e.g., Minglewood > Friend of the Devil, Crazy Fingers > Miracle) create a quirky, almost psychic pacing that feels off‑beat to some listeners.
